kurz: When wheat flour is kneaded with water, two proteins link into an elastic network: gluten.
bild_im_kopf: Like a net made of chewing gum: the more you pull and fold it, the tougher and stretchier it gets. A strong net holds gas bubbles like a balloon.
was_passiert: Flour contains two proteins, glutenin and gliadin. With water they bond, and through kneading or a long rest they line up into long, stretchy strands. Glutenin gives strength, gliadin makes it stretchy. Fat and sugar slow the network down, salt tightens it.
warum_wichtig: Bread needs a lot of gluten for its holes and chew. Cakes, shortcrust and pancakes need little so they stay tender.
faustregeln: Bread: knead for a long time or rest for a long time. Time replaces kneading.
Cakes and muffins: only stir until the flour has disappeared.
Fat and sugar slow the network down. That is why shortcrust is short.
Dough that springs back needs a rest; then it can be rolled out.

praxis.text: Strong network wanted: knead until it passes the [[fenstertest|windowpane test]], or use a long cold prove.
Little network wanted: stir briefly, use cold butter and little water.
Pasta dough needs a firm network for bite: knead it and rest it for half an hour.

mythos.behauptung: Bread dough has to be kneaded long and hard.
mythos.richtig: It does not. If the dough rests overnight, the proteins line up by themselves. That is how no-knead bread works.
